title: Matching the Training-Time Weight Rule in Inference-Time Expert Deactivation
abstract: arXiv:2611.05804v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Expert deactivation at inference time changes both token routing and expert weights, and its effect on performance depends on how these changes are implemented. We compare removal, freezing, remaining-expert renormalization, and unnormalized re-routing on identical disabled sets across five instruction-tuned checkpoints from four model families, with a base OLMoE checkpoint as an additional comparison. We develop a weight-sum model that relates the loss of expert contributions and changes in branch scale to the weight rule used during training. With half of the experts deactivated according to activation-based rankings, remaining-expert renormalization yields the highest perplexity in models trained with raw router probabilities, whereas unnormalized re-routing yields the highest perplexity in models trained with normalized weights. tldr: 该论文提出一个权重和模型，揭示推理时专家停用方法应与训练时的权重规则相匹配——使用原始路由概率训练的模型适合剩余专家重归一化，而使用归一化权重训练的模型则适合未归一化重新路由。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a weight-sum model showing that inference-time expert deactivation should match the training-time weight rule: remaining-expert renormalization performs best for models trained with raw router probabilities, while unnormalized re-routing suits models trained with normalized weights.
